name: Kid Dynamite
label: Jade Tree
lede: Two ex-Lifetime guys, a singer headed for film school and 38 songs in under an hour: Kid Dynamite lasted barely two years and spent the next thirteen being begged to come back.

eras.title: Out of Lifetime, into Philly
eras.text: When Lifetime fell apart, guitarist Dan Yemin and drummer Dave Wagenschutz kept going in Philadelphia. With singer Jason Shevchuk they made a faster, rawer band, and Jade Tree had its debut out within six months of the first show.

years.h: Dan Yemin and Dave Wagenschutz start Kid Dynamite in Philadelphia
years.p: Both came straight from [[Lifetime|c9329809-8510-45b9-9202-5640398ddaee]]. Steve Ferrell took the bass.

years.h: Six Songs with Jay Singing: the Kid Dynamite demo tape
years.p: The self-released cassette introduced singer [[Jason Shevchuk|9edfdd52-046b-4c72-98c5-2fe2bb2b046c]].

years.h: First Kid Dynamite show: opening for Better Than a Thousand
years.p: Kid Dynamite debuted in Philadelphia on April 22, 1998, supporting [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]], the band of Youth of Today's Ray Cappo.

years.h: Kid Dynamite plays its first run of East Coast shows
years.p: A summer of East Coast dates before the band went into the studio.

years.h: Kid Dynamite: 20 songs in 27 minutes, Jade Tree JT1039
years.p: Recorded in September 1998 at Trax East in South River NJ with [[Steve Evetts|ae091a4c-0a25-4555-8874-5f05768d9d18]], who had produced Lifetime. Several songs don't reach two minutes.

eras.title: Shorter, faster, gone
eras.text: Kid Dynamite toured hard, swapped bass players twice and cut a second album in seventeen days. Then the singer left for film school and the band played its last shows the same month the record came out.

years.h: Kid Dynamite splits with 88 Fingers Louie and I Stand Alone
years.p: A split on Sub City (SC004) with Chicago's [[88 Fingers Louie|2cf874cd-6bb2-49a3-956a-a7228e7a317f]], and another on I Stand Alone Records.

years.h: Steve Ferrell leaves Kid Dynamite; Ernie Parada fills in on bass
years.p: [[Ernie Parada|586bfe03-6a6f-4aa5-bac8-d2f97d2acfb6]] covered bass temporarily before Michael "Spider" Cotterman took the job for good.

years.h: Coast to coast opening for Good Riddance, with In My Eyes
years.p: Kid Dynamite spent summer 1999 crossing the US as openers for [[Good Riddance|ab4725b8-7a2f-429a-a55a-3dde07c9acea]], alongside Boston's [[In My Eyes|f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d]].

years.h: Shorter, Faster, Louder tracked in 17 days at Trax East
years.p: Steve Evetts again. [[Dave Hause|feb265ec-e510-4277-9451-914e3c6ceac5]] sang backups and Ernie Parada added vocals.

years.h: Kid Dynamite plays with Kill Your Idols, Snapcase and Buried Alive
years.p: Late-1999 shows alongside [[Kill Your Idols|b6154aed-416f-43bf-93fe-0906b051535f]], [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]] and Buried Alive.

years.h: Jason Shevchuk quits Kid Dynamite for film school
years.p: Kid Dynamite's singer left in December 1999 to study film. The band chose to end rather than replace him.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes Right Brigade's Jesse Standhard was rumored as a replacement, but it was never confirmed and never happened.

Leaving at the peak is exactly what fixed the band in people's memories: two records, no decline.

years.h: Last shows: two nights at Philly's First Unitarian Church
years.p: Kid Dynamite said goodbye in the church basement that anchored Philadelphia punk, on February 18 and 19, 2000.

years.h: Shorter, Faster, Louder arrives as the band ends
years.p: Eighteen songs in 24:49 on Jade Tree. Exclaim! heard early Minor Threat and 7 Seconds in songs like Living Daylights and Death and Taxes.
years.xp:
CMJ New Music Report called it a punk rock marathon built for moshing until the audience drops. Nuvo went further and called it genre-defining.

Wikipedia's band page dates the release to February 15, 2000; the album page says February 29.

eras.title: Benefits, a DVD and new bands
eras.text: The members scattered into Paint It Black, Good Riddance and None More Black, but kept reuniting for causes. Jade Tree kept the catalog alive with a rarities disc and a documentary.

years.h: Dan Yemin steps up to the mic in Paint It Black
years.p: Yemin formed [[Paint It Black|90910a44-7579-4730-9499-0546159fe4e3]] in Philadelphia in 2002, on vocals, with Dave Wagenschutz on drums until 2006.

years.h: Three Philly reunion shows raise $20,000 for the Savio Endowment
years.p: Kid Dynamite came back for three Philadelphia benefits for the Syrentha J. Savio Endowment, raising $20,000.

years.h: Cheap Shots, Youth Anthems gathers the rarities
years.p: Jade Tree (JT1085) compiled the demos, split and comp tracks into one disc.

years.h: Kid Dynamite plays CBGB to help save it
years.p: A New York benefit for the historic Bowery club, the day after Lifetime's reunion weekend ended.

years.h: Four Years in One Gulp: the Kid Dynamite documentary
years.p: Jade Tree (JT1108) released the DVD documentary of a band that had barely lasted two years.

eras.title: One more time, for good this time
eras.text: A 39-song tribute album proved the demand, and Kid Dynamite spent four years playing festivals from Philadelphia to Austin. In 2013 it closed the book at This Is Hardcore.

years.h: Carry the Torch: a 39-song Kid Dynamite tribute
years.p: Get Outta Town Records gathered punk and hardcore bands to cover the catalog, more songs than the band had released.

years.h: Kid Dynamite reunites at This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia
years.p: Jade Tree put out a This Is Hardcore release on August 15, 2010; Punknews ran it as Kid Dynamite: Live from This Is Hardcore.

years.h: FYF Fest, The Fest and Fun Fun Fun Fest in one fall
years.p: Kid Dynamite played Fuck Yeah Fest in Los Angeles, then The Fest 10 in Gainesville and FunFunFunFest in Austin.

years.h: Kid Dynamite ends for good at This Is Hardcore 2013
years.p: The final run: This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia plus New York shows with [[Swearin'|5b62be91-b158-40a7-a51d-43b1a3b91ec3]] and [[Joyce Manor|945d3b69-27cd-45fa-b491-52553a63dead]]. Punknews headlined it: for good, this time.
